name: Keeper strip on Today
hostSurface: The unified Today tab on each platform — NOT the doc's named targets (HubTodayCard is mounted only at /app/hub, which is not a tab, and the native kicker belongs to the push-only briefing screen).
purpose: Give the return surface a face: who is looking after this address, what is due, and how much the place file knows.
contents: Species avatar (6 species x 4 moods), name, mood word, the mood line verbatim ('Nothing due this week.' / 'Recycling tomorrow.' / 'A bill is overdue.'), and the fact count as a tap target into the place file. Requires a nullable keeper block on the Today payload, since mood is computed in GET /api/hub — a third payload neither Today fetches.
states: loading (reserved space, no pop-in after the weather renders)
unnamed (generic silhouette + 'Give your place a keeper')
MOOD UNAVAILABLE — 'Couldn't check what's due', visually distinct from relaxed
T1 saved place (calendar-only mood; copy says 'this place', never 'household')
alert on screen (avatar and mood suppressed; the alert owns the screen)
visualization: Avatar + name + mood line as one strip above the weather. The fact count renders as a five-segment ring of CATEGORIES (place, dates, money, people, proof) filled where anything is known, integer inside — deliberately not a progress bar or percentage, so nothing reads as '60% complete' and a saved place reads as a smaller instrument rather than a failing one.
uxNote: Two changes to the doc. (1) Ship it on the Today each platform actually shows, or almost nobody sees it. (2) Mood must be nullable end to end: the inputs come from hub.js:221-260, whose Mail and bill counts are wrapped in .catch(() => 0) over column names that can fail, so a broken query renders as a cheerful 'relaxed' on the day a bill is overdue — a lie on the one metric the pilot scores at zero. Drop the 'knows N things' mechanic as a growth game; the place file already shows the facts.
